slides.title: The listing image test
slides.subtitle: One storage box. Two search images.
slides.caption: percentage points in click-through rate
slides.notes: Fictional seven-day search experiment. Decide whether to expand the wardrobe image test.

slides.title: The same product in two settings
slides.subtitle: Visitors stayed in one group. Each image received 20,000 impressions at the same price.
slides.notes: The listing title, offer and detail page were identical. Both variants ran for seven days. These are AI-generated product images.

slides.title: The wardrobe image earned more clicks
slides.subtitle: With equal impressions, the wardrobe image drew 900 clicks and the white background drew 720.
slides.note: Click-through rate = product clicks ÷ search impressions. The absolute difference is 0.9 percentage points.
slides.notes: 720 / 20,000 = 3.6%. 900 / 20,000 = 4.5%. A visitor may generate multiple impressions.

slides.title: Both images converted 5% of clicks
slides.subtitle: The wardrobe image generated 45 attributed orders, compared with 36 for the white background.
slides.asideLabel: additional orders with the wardrobe image
slides.note: Orders are attributed within 24 hours of a click, including clicks on the final day.
slides.notes: Orders per click: 36 / 720 and 45 / 900. The case does not include revenue or return data.

slides.title: Expand the wardrobe test for one week
slides.subtitle: Keep a white-background control for this product before changing the listing for everyone.
